title: Duplicating a Node in the editor fails when it has tool-generated, owned children with children
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: Godot 4.6.1.stable, Godot 4.6.stable, Godot 4.5.1.stable, Godot 4.5.stable - Not reproducible in: Unknown ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8129) - AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M (16 threads) - 15.28 GiB memory ### Issue description I've created an inherited scene from a 3D mesh that has a @tool script, and one child node (the MeshInstance3D, with a collider). The attached script takes the child mesh instance, duplicates it a number of times (according to a property), and adds the copies as children. It then sets these children's `owner` property to `self`. At this point, when adding the scene, I can click on the visual child instances, and it will select the parent node. This is because of the `owner` assignment. However, also due to assigning `owner`, along with having a collider, it appears I can no longer duplicate the node. I get an error: ``` ERROR: Node not found: "@MeshInstance3D@83293" (relative to "MySceneName"). ERROR: Failed to duplicate node. ERROR: editor/docks/scene_tree_dock.cpp:956 - Condition "!dup" is true. Continuing. ``` It appears that, maybe, because the node has children with the scene root as owner, it thinks they also need to be copied. ----- Related error: If there is no collider, duplicating the node 'works', but the console does spit out an error twice: ``` ERROR: scene/main/node.cpp:1849 - Index p_index = 1 is out of bounds ((int)data.children_cache.size() - data.internal_children_front_count_cache - data.internal_children_back_count_cache = 1). ERROR: Child node disappeared while duplicating. ERROR: scene/main/node.cpp:1849 - Index p_index = 1 is out of bounds ((int)data.children_cache.size() - data.internal_children_front_count_cache - data.internal_children_back_count_cache = 1). ERROR: Child node disappeared while duplicating. ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a model in Blender *with a collider* (issue doesn't occur without a collider), and export (as .glb in this case). 2. Create an inherited scene from the .glb with a script that copies the mesh and *sets the copy's `owner` to `self`* (see script below). 3. Drop it into another scene. 4. Try duplicating it. The required conditions that cause the issue to occur are italicized above: 1. The child that is getting copied must, itself, have children (in this case a collider). 2. The `owner` of the copied children must be assigned to the parent node. ----- Example script (from MRP): ```gdscript @tool class_name CubeArray extends Node3D @export_range(1, 10) var count: int = 1: get: return count set(n): count = n; update() @onready var cube: MeshInstance3D = $Cube var copies: Array[MeshInstance3D] = [] func _ready() -> void: copies.append(cube) update() func update() -> void: if !is_node_ready(): return while copies.size() < count: var copy = cube.duplicate() copies.append(copy) add_child(copy) copy.owner = self # <----------------- while copies.size() > count: var copy = copies.pop_back() remove_child(copy) copy.queue_free() for i in copies.size(): copies[i].position.x = i * 3 ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) For reproducing this issue: - Open the attached project. - Open up the `main.tscn` scene. - Select one of the cube arrays. - Try duplicating (Ctrl/Cmd-D) or copying (Ctrl/Cmd-C). [issue-report.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25639959/issue-report.zip)
